steering_ledger.verbatim:
"LFM2.5-2.6B (https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm2-5-2-6b) is a plausible inexpensive agent candidate, but “without restrictions” conflicts with
    the released model license’s $10M annual-revenue threshold." - who cares. We're not building for commercial purposes. This seems like a very promising candidate to replace gemma4 as worker_general.

"Prime Agent (https://www.primeintellect.ai/blog/prime-agent) contains useful persistence and recovery patterns, but its Factorio experiment
    explicitly reward-hacked the environment and converted the exploit into reusable skills. The related Continual Harness
    (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09998) should therefore remain a shadow-mode proposal mechanism behind existing keep/revert gates." - looking forward to the deep dive on this to see what can be exported/merged from it into our stack.

  "The Pokee-Isaac report (https://console.pokee.ai/pokee-isaac-28b-v0-technical-report.pdf) is relevant but presently proprietary and
    non-reproducible. Its B200 results do not transfer to MI210, and several comparisons mix model failures with endpoint, harness, and
    infrastructure failures." - yes, I'm aware but was wondering whether any functionalities can be independently re-engineered by us for our own purposes.

"  - VerMem (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03137) substantially improves memory-evaluation methodology, but its public repository implements
    rule-based verifiers rather than the paper’s load-bearing DeepSeek semantic verifiers." - looking forward to this deep dive also. I'm sure more itneresting material will surface.

proceed with recommended dives

"LFM2.5-2.6B (https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B) is a credible worker_general challenger. The noncommercial license use is not a
    blocker; frozen v8 already supports LFM2 loading and its specialized tool-call syntax. The real gate is a direct Q4_K_M comparison against
    Gemma4 26B-A4B, including mandatory-reasoning overhead, tool compliance, task success, memory, and wall time." - at such a small model size, we should test Q8 also.

"Prime Agent (https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent) contributes two concrete missing invariants: a process-safe session lease
    and an uncertain-side-effect recovery journal. Most other persistence, scheduling, rollback, and optimization features overlap existing
    EPYC capabilities.

  - Continual Harness (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09998) belongs in shadow proposal generation behind existing keep/revert gates. Its
    implementation lacks held-out acceptance, transactional rollback, reward-hacking protection, and a genuine sandbox. The 842-repeat
    invalid-tool loop and Factorio exploit make excellent adversarial fixtures." - interesting.

"- Pokee-Isaac (https://console.pokee.ai/pokee-isaac-28b-v0-technical-report.pdf) yields clean-room implementable evaluation/service patterns:
    joint long-context quality and serving metrics, typed failure attribution, same-harness security evaluation, scoped tools, resumable
    sessions, sandboxing, and trace replay. Its 10M-context architecture cannot be reconstructed from the report." - so there are no hints that we could use to speculate as to how they enable 10M context windows? Is it a REPL trick of some kind? I'm still of the opinion that working with a REPL and focusing and yper-precise tool calls is the most efficient way to proceed.

"VerMem (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03137) materially improves memory evaluation over Cognitive Workspace. Its operation, provenance,
    version, rollback, and tombstone schemas are worth prototyping in shadow traces. The released rule-based verifiers cannot support the
    paper’s reported semantic-verifier gains." - lets take/implement everythign we can get.
   "  Stage 2 surfaced five recommended follow-up sources:

  1. Official LFM GGUF repository (https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B-GGUF) — fixes the exact deployment artifact.
  2. Continual Harness implementation (https://github.com/sethkarten/continual-harness) — establishes actual proposal, persistence, and sandbox
     behavior.

  3. DTAP (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04808) — primary security-evaluation contract behind Pokee’s confounded comparison.
  4. Mem0 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19413) — production-oriented cross-session persistence/deletion comparator.
  5. Memory-R1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.19828) — direct RL memory-management comparator for VerMem’s operation-level credit." -  proceed with depp diving  all five of the recommended literature expansion.
